# First-Aid Checklist: Chemical Burn

## Immediate Actions (First Few Minutes)

- [ ] **Ensure your own safety** — wear gloves or protect yourself before touching the victim
- [ ] **Remove the person from the chemical source** if safe to do so
- [ ] **Call emergency services (911)** or have someone else call
- [ ] **Identify the chemical** if possible (check container labels, safety data sheets) — tell paramedics

## Remove Contaminants

- [ ] **Remove jewelry, watches, and clothing** near the burn — chemicals can get trapped underneath
- [ ] **Brush off dry powder chemicals** (like lime) with a gloved hand or cloth *before* rinsing — water may activate some dry chemicals
- [ ] **Do not** wipe or rub the affected area

## Flush the Burn

- [ ] **Rinse with cool running water for at least 20 minutes** (or until paramedics arrive)
- [ ] Hold the affected area under a gentle stream of water, or pour water over it
- [ ] Keep water flowing **away from unaffected areas** so runoff doesn't spread the chemical
- [ ] For eye burns: flush the eye continuously, holding eyelids open; rinse from the inner corner outward
- [ ] **Do not** use hot water, ice, or neutralizing agents (baking soda, vinegar) unless directed by poison control

## Protect and Monitor

- [ ] **Loosely cover the burn** with a clean, dry cloth or sterile non-stick dressing (avoid tight wrapping)
- [ ] **Do not** apply ointments, creams, butter, or home remedies
- [ ] **Keep the person warm and comfortable** — cover them with a blanket (avoid the burned area)
- [ ] **Monitor for shock**: pale/clammy skin, rapid breathing, dizziness — lay the person down and elevate their legs if needed
- [ ] **Watch breathing** — be prepared to perform CPR if the person stops breathing

## While Waiting for Paramedics

- [ ] Continue flushing if pain persists
- [ ] Keep the person calm and still
- [ ] Note the time of exposure and how long flushing has occurred
- [ ] Have the chemical container or label ready to show responders
- [ ] Do **not** give food or drink

## Special Warnings

⚠️ **Call poison control (1-800-222-1222 in the US)** if the chemical is unknown or unusual
⚠️ **Seek immediate help** if the burn is large, deep, on the face/eyes/genitals, or the person shows breathing difficulty
⚠️ **Never delay flushing** to look for information — rinse first, identify later
